subject: Meteorology
title: Altostratus Clouds
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Altostratus Clouds.

hook.text: Altostratus is a gray or blue-gray veil at mid-level—thin enough to show a blurry Sun, like frosted glass.

buildup.text: These clouds form between 2 and 7 km, usually ahead of an approaching warm front.

discovery.text: Seeing altostratus often means rain is coming within 12 to 24 hours as the front gets closer.

twist.text: Unlike cirrostratus, altostratus doesn't produce halos—it's too thick for ice-crystal optics.

climax.text: As the front nears, altostratus thickens into nimbostratus—and the steady rain begins.

punchline.text: A hazy Sun through gray sky? Rain is on its way.
